results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** The finite-dimensional data and conventions in the Statement. For analytic interpretations, use only the conditional projective GAGA interface in [F3]; no analytic family algebraization is assumed.

[F1] The raw ADHM equations, stability, costability and torus conventions are exactly those of the local definition. [[def-qftx-adhm-linear-data-stability-and-regularity]]

[F2] The stable complex quotient has word-frame charts, is a geometric quotient, and has tangent space $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$. [[lem-adhm-stable-quotient-and-torus-lift]]

[F3] The preceding lemma supplies the exact P² diagonal monad and its framed vanishings under the stated cohomology/base-change assumptions; its algebraic/analytic interface is conditional on the unresolved analytic package recorded there. [[lem-qftx-p2-beilinson-diagonal-and-framed-vanishing]]

[F4] At positive real FI, stable complex orbits correspond to the real unitary quotient; at zero FI the real unitary quotient corresponds exactly to stable and costable data. [[thm-qftx-adhm-real-complex-quotient-correspondence]]

[F5] The coherent-sheaf Serre pairing for $H^2$ and the projective twisting-sheaf cohomology have the exact P² hypotheses used here. [[thm-serre-duality-projective-space-coherent-sheaves]], [[thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]]

[F6] A commuting pair of complex endomorphisms of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space has a common eigenvector. [[thm-the-complex-numbers-are-algebraically-closed]]

[F7] For a nonzero finite module of projective dimension at most one over a regular local surface ring, the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula gives depth at least one. Such a module has no nonzero finite-length submodule; torsion-freeness additionally requires excluding torsion supported in dimension one, as checked in step 3.1. [[thm-auslander-buchsbaum-serre-regularity-criterion]]

[F8] For a finite module over a Noetherian local algebra, if its residue fiber is flat over the residue field and the maximal-ideal multiplication map is injective, then it is flat over the base local ring; vanishing of the residue-field Tor group gives that injection. [[lem-noetherian-local-flatness-criterion-finite-over-target]]



**Given:** The Statement's data. Let $k>0$ until the separate $k=0$ check.

1.1 Direct multiplication gives $\beta\alpha=(-z_0B_2+z_2)(z_0B_1-z_1)+(z_0B_1-z_1)(z_0B_2-z_2)+z_0^2IJ=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$. The $z_0z_1$ and $z_0z_2$ cross terms cancel pairwise, and the $z_1z_2$ terms cancel. On $L_\infty$, $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ is injective at every point because $z_1,z_2$ are not simultaneously zero. Thus $\alpha$ has full rank generically; its sheaf kernel is a torsion subsheaf of the locally free source, and hence is zero. [F1, algebra]

1.2 Conversely, let $\mathcal E$ be a framed torsion-free sheaf with the stated Hilbert polynomial. The preceding Beilinson lemma constructs its monad, with terms $V_1\mathcal O(-1)$, $M\mathcal O$, and $V_2\mathcal O(1)$ of ranks $k,2k+N,k$. Its restriction to $L_\infty$ remains exact at the ends because $\mathcal E$ is locally free there. Put $K=\ker\beta|_{L_\infty}$. The sequence $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to W\mathcal O\to0$ splits since $\operatorname{Ext}^1(W\mathcal O,V_1\mathcal O(-1))=V_1\otimes W^*\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$. [F3, F5]

2.1 At a point of $L_\infty$, $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,0)$ is onto. At an affine point $[1:u_1:u_2]$, failure of surjectivity would give a nonzero $\lambda\in V^*$ with $\lambda B_1=u_1\lambda$, $\lambda B_2=u_2\lambda$, and $\lambda I=0$. Then $\lambda$ annihilates every vector $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, contradicting stability. Hence $\beta$ is everywhere onto, so $K=\ker\beta$ is a vector bundle of rank $k+N$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 A fiber kernel of $\alpha$ over $[1:u_1:u_2]$ is a nonzero vector $v$ with $B_1v=u_1v$, $B_2v=u_2v$, and $Jv=0$. Each $u_i$ must be an eigenvalue of the fixed matrix $B_i$, so the rank-drop locus is contained in the finite product of the two finite spectra. Such a vector spans a common invariant line in $\ker J$, so costability fails. Conversely, if costability fails, choose a nonzero common invariant subspace $S\subseteq\ker J$. On $S$, the complex equation implies $[B_1,B_2]|_S=-IJ|_S=0$, so the restrictions commute. By [F6] they have a common eigenvector; its eigenvalues give an affine point where $\alpha$ has a fiber kernel. Therefore $\alpha$ has full fiber rank everywhere exactly for costable data. [F1, F6, step 1.1, algebra]

2.3 The remaining line extension $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\oplus W\mathcal O\to M\mathcal O\to V_2\mathcal O(1)\to0$ has class in $\operatorname{Hom}(V_2,V_1)\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$, since $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Twist by $\mathcal O(-1)$ and take cohomology. The connecting map $V_2\to V_1\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$ is an isomorphism: the adjacent groups $H^0(\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))$ vanish, while $H^1(\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C$. Thus $V_2$ is identified with $V_1$ by this canonical extension class. Choosing a basis of $V_1$ and using the fixed framed basis of $W$ identifies $M=V\oplus V\oplus W$ and the line maps with the two Euler blocks in the Statement. Any other such choice differs by one simultaneous element of $GL(V)$. [F3, F5, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 The sequence $0\to V\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{\alpha}K\to\mathcal E\to0$ has locally free first two terms. Away from the finite rank-drop set of step 2.2, $\mathcal E$ is locally free; hence any torsion is supported at finitely many points. At such a point, the local ring is regular of dimension two and this sequence gives $\operatorname{pd}\mathcal E\le1$. The Auslander–Buchsbaum formula [F7] gives $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal E\ge1$. A nonzero finite-length torsion submodule would force depth zero, so no such torsion exists. Thus $\mathcal E$ is torsion-free of rank $(2k+N)-k-k=N$. The rank drops only off $L_\infty$, so $\mathcal E$ is locally free near the framing line. [F7, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.2 The remaining coefficients of the two linear maps are their $z_0$ coefficients, so write $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0C_1+z_2,z_0C_2-z_1,z_0I)$. The coefficients of $z_0z_1$ and $z_0z_2$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ force $C_1=B_2$ and $C_2=B_1$; the $z_0^2$ coefficient is then $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. This recovers the stated ADHM form. The surjectivity of $\beta$ implies stability: if $U=\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(W)\}$ were proper, it is invariant and the induced $B_1,B_2$ on $V/U$ commute because $[B_1,B_2]=-IJ$ has image in $U$. Their dual actions on the nonzero annihilator $U^\perp\subset V^*$ commute, so [F6] gives a common eigen-covector $\lambda\ne0$ with $\lambda I=0$. At the corresponding affine point, $\lambda\beta=0$, contradicting surjectivity. [F1, F3, F6, step 2.1, step 2.3, algebra]

4.1 On $L_\infty$, the complex is $0\to V\mathcal O_{L_\infty}(-1)\xrightarrow{(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T}(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O_{L_\infty}\xrightarrow{(z_2,-z_1,0)}V\mathcal O_{L_\infty}(1)\to0$. The first two $V$ summands form the Euler resolution of the zero sheaf on the line, while the $W$ summand passes unchanged to middle cohomology. The framing is therefore the canonical identification $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}=W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. In the Grothendieck group, the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=[(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O]-[V\mathcal O(-1)]-[V\mathcal O(1)]$. Taking Euler characteristics after twisting by $\mathcal O(m)$ and using $\chi(\mathcal O(d))=\binom{d+2}{2}$ yields $\chi(\mathcal E(m))=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$. [F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 The Beilinson construction is natural under framed sheaf isomorphisms, so an isomorphism of framed sheaves induces maps on the cohomology vector spaces used in steps 1.2–6.2 and hence a single change of basis $g\in GL(V)$; the normalized Euler blocks force the recovered tuples to differ by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)$. Conversely such a $g$ is an isomorphism of monads acting trivially on $W$, and therefore induces a framed sheaf isomorphism. This proves the pointwise inverse equivalence modulo $GL(V)$. For a finite-type data family, step 2.1 makes $\beta$ surjective on the total space, so $K=\ker\beta$ is locally free. The sequence $0\to V\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to\mathcal E\to0$ is exact and its terms before $\mathcal E$ are flat over the base. After tensoring with any residue field of the base, the first map remains sheaf-injective by step 1.1; hence $\operatorname{Tor}_1(k(s),\mathcal E)=0$. Since $\mathcal E$ is finite over each local ring of $\mathbb P^2\times S$ and its residue fiber is a vector space over the residue field, [F8] gives flatness over $S$. Under the stated relative cohomology and base-change hypotheses, the same constructions use vector bundles and are inverse for families. [F2, F3, F8, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 2.3, step 3.2, algebra]

4.3 Step 2.2 proves that costability is equivalent to fiberwise injectivity of $\alpha$. Since $\beta$ is surjective and $K$ is locally free, the quotient $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is locally free exactly when $\alpha$ has constant full rank; failure at any point gives a fiber dimension jump. Hence the locally-free sheaf locus is precisely the regular ADHM locus. Combining this with [F4] gives the positive-FI and zero-FI identifications in the Statement. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1]

5.1 Apply the family equivalence to $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A first-order deformation of the ADHM data is $(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)$ satisfying $d\mu_{\mathbb C}=0$; infinitesimal changes of basis are $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$. Differentiating the monad gives the chain perturbation $(\dot\alpha,\dot\beta)$ with $\beta\dot\alpha+\dot\beta\alpha=0$, and a change by $d_0(\xi)$ is the corresponding chain homotopy. Since the family construction and its inverse commute with this dual-number base change, they induce inverse linear maps on first-order framed deformations and on the quotient tangent spaces $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$. [F2, F3, step 4.2, algebra]

5.2 Let the rotation torus act on homogeneous coordinates with characters $1,t_1,t_2$, and let $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$ act on $W$. On the monad vector spaces choose characters $V(t_1t_2)^{-1}$ in the source, $Vt_2^{-1}\oplus Vt_1^{-1}\oplus Wh$ in the middle, and $V$ in the target, with the natural linearizations of $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(1)$. The first and second blocks are equivariant because the ratios of middle to source characters are respectively $t_1,t_2$; the $J$ block has ratio $t_1t_2h$; in $\beta$, the first two ratios are $t_2,t_1$ and the framing block ratio is $h^{-1}$. These are exactly the raw transformations in [F1]. On $L_\infty$ the Euler blocks cancel, leaving the framing factor $Wh$; its character is $\sum_a e_a^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_a e_a$. Thus the monad correspondence is torus-equivariant in the specified dual-framing convention. [F1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 If $k=0$, $V=0$, all four maps and both equations are the unique zero-dimensional maps, stability and costability are vacuous, and the monad is $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its middle cohomology is the framed bundle $W\mathcal O$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}$. Conversely, [F3] constructs this same zero-term monad from every framed sheaf with that polynomial, so the framing identifies each such sheaf with $W\mathcal O$. Thus both moduli spaces are points, and all empty-matrix and Euler-block conventions are satisfied. [F1, F3, F5, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The sheaf, framing, Hilbert polynomial and AC in the Statement. For the proof's algebraic/analytic family comparison, use the exact conditional GAGA interface of [F1]; that supplier itself remains escalated until its analytic package is locally supplied.

[F1] Conditional GAGA on projective spaces: analytification is exact, preserves cohomology and Ext, and commutes with restriction to $L_\infty$; its use here is limited to algebraic-family fiber comparison under the base-change hypotheses in the Statement. [[thm-qftx-projective-gaga-for-monad-data]]

[F2] The Koszul complex of a section whose zero scheme is a regular codimension-two subscheme resolves its structure sheaf, and exactness persists under the stated flat fiber restriction. [[lem-koszul-resolution-and-flat-fibre-restriction]]

[F3] The hypercohomology spectral sequences for the bounded filtered complexes converge to their total hypercohomology with the stated edge and filtration maps; their comparisons are available under DC, which follows from AC. [[thm-first-hypercohomology-spectral-sequence]], [[thm-second-hypercohomology-spectral-sequence]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F4] For coherent $\mathcal F$ on $\mathbb P^2$, $H^2(\mathcal F)^*\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal O(-3))$, with the coherent-sheaf Ext interpretation. [[thm-serre-duality-projective-space-coherent-sheaves]]

[F5] The twisting-sheaf cohomology, finite twisted locally-free resolutions and projective-bundle diagonal $K$-class generator have the stated projective hypotheses. [[thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]], [[lem-coherent-sheaf-finite-twisted-locally-free-resolution-projective-space]], [[lem-relative-projective-bundle-k-theory-generators]]

[F6] If a finite module over a Noetherian local algebra has flat residue fiber and the maximal-ideal multiplication map is injective, it is flat over the base local ring. [[lem-noetherian-local-flatness-criterion-finite-over-target]]

[F7] Every finitely generated torsion-free module over a principal ideal domain is free. [[cor-finitely-generated-torsion-free-modules-over-a-pid-are-free]]

[F8] Nakayama's lemma: a finite module over a local ring is zero if its maximal-ideal multiple equals the module. [[thm-nakayama-lemma]]

[F9] On a regular Noetherian surface, the double dual of a rank-one exterior power is a line bundle and determinant maps extend across codimension two. [[lem-regular-surface-reflexive-modules-and-codimension-one-lattices]]

[A1] The family clause assumes the locally free cohomology and base-change maps specified in the Statement. It does not assert base change when those maps fail to be isomorphisms.



**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement; all sheaf cohomology below is algebraic unless explicitly analytified.

1.1 Near a point of $L_\infty$, let $R$ be the regular local surface ring, $t$ a local equation of $L_\infty$, and $M$ the torsion-free stalk of $\mathcal E$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective on $M$. Lift a basis of $M/tM\cong(R/(t))^N$ to obtain a surjection $R^N\twoheadrightarrow M$ by Nakayama [F8]. If $K$ is its kernel, tensoring with $R/(t)$ is exact on the left because $t$ is injective on $M$; the lifted basis makes $(R/(t))^N\to M/tM$ an isomorphism, so $K/tK=0$. Nakayama [F8] gives $K=0$, proving local freeness of rank $N$ near the framed line. [F8, given, algebra]

1.2 Let $Q$ be the universal rank-two quotient bundle on the first factor. The section of $\mathcal O(1)$ on the second factor tensored with $Q$ on the first, induced by the second tautological line modulo the first, vanishes exactly on the diagonal. In affine coordinates transverse to the diagonal its two components are a regular parameter pair; hence its Koszul complex is exact and resolves $\mathcal O_\Delta$. Since $\det Q=\mathcal O(1)$ and $Q^*=\Omega^1(1)$, the resolution is $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(-2)\to\Omega^1(1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\boxtimes\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\Delta\to0$. The regularity check is local along the diagonal, and outside it one component is a unit; this verifies exactness at every point. Its alternating $K$-class is the diagonal generator from [F5], but here the actual Koszul complex, rather than only its $K$-class, supplies the resolution. [F2, F5, algebra]

2.1 The framing makes $\det\mathcal E$ trivial on $L_\infty$, so $c_1(\mathcal E)\cdot L_\infty=0$ and $\mu(\mathcal E)=0$. For a positive-rank subsheaf $\mathcal F\subset\mathcal E$, replace it by its saturation. At the generic point of $L_\infty$, use the chart $z_1\ne0$ with coordinates $x=z_0/z_1$, $y=z_2/z_1$; the local ring is $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x)}$, a discrete valuation ring because every nonzero polynomial is a power of $x$ times a polynomial not divisible by $x$, and the latter is a unit after localization. Saturation makes both $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal E/\mathcal F$ torsion-free there, hence free by [F7]. Thus reducing the inclusion modulo $x$ remains injective at that generic point. Taking the double dual of its top exterior power gives a morphism from the determinant line of $\mathcal F$ to the corresponding exterior power of $\mathcal E$ near the line; [F9] makes this extension a morphism across the finite non-locally-free set. It is nonzero at the generic point and therefore restricts to a nonzero map $\det(\mathcal F)|_{L_\infty}\to\bigwedge^{\mathrm{rk}\mathcal F}(W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty})$. Some component into a trivial line bundle is a nonzero section of $(\det(\mathcal F)|_{L_\infty})^*$, forcing $\deg(\det(\mathcal F)|_{L_\infty})\le0$. This proves slope-semistability of $\mathcal E$ of slope zero. [F7, F9, given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 A nonzero section of $\mathcal E(-d)$ for $d=1,2$ would give a rank-one subsheaf of $\mathcal E$ whose determinant has degree at least $d>0$, contrary to step 2.1. Hence $H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. A nonzero map $\mathcal E\to\mathcal O(-d)$ for $d=1,2$ would have a torsion-free image that is a quotient of $\mathcal E$ of slope at least zero: its kernel is a subsheaf of the slope-zero semistable sheaf, so has degree at most zero, while $\deg\mathcal E=0$. The same image is a subsheaf of $\mathcal O(-d)$ of degree at most $-d$. This is impossible. By coherent Serre duality [F4], these Hom vanishings give $H^2(\mathcal E(-1))=H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. [F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The Hilbert polynomial gives $\chi(\mathcal E(-1))=\chi(\mathcal E(-2))=-k$. With the vanishings of step 3.1, $h^1(\mathcal E(-1))=h^1(\mathcal E(-2))=k$. The Euler sequence is locally split, so tensoring it by $\mathcal E$ remains exact; its first map therefore injects $H^0(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)$ into $H^0(\mathcal E(-1))^3$, which is zero by step 3.1. [F5, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Serre duality identifies $H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)^*$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal E,T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3))$. The twisted Euler sequence is $0\to\mathcal O(-3-d)\to\mathcal O(-2-d)^3\to T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3-d)\to0$. For $d\ge-1$, both $H^0$ terms on the left vanish and $H^1(\mathcal O(-3-d))=0$ by [F5], hence $H^0(T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3-d))=0$. Any rank-one torsion-free subsheaf of $T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3)$ of degree at least $-1$ would extend by double dual to a nonzero map $\mathcal O(d)\to T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3)$ for some $d\ge-1$, a contradiction. Thus $T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3)$ is stable of slope $-3/2$. A nonzero map from the slope-zero semistable $\mathcal E$ to this stable sheaf would have image both a quotient of slope at least zero and a subsheaf of negative slope, impossible. Consequently $H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=0$. From the Euler sequence and the Hilbert polynomial, $\chi(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=3\chi(\mathcal E(-1))-\chi(\mathcal E)=-(2k+N)$, so $h^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=2k+N$. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Tensor this resolution on its first factor by $\mathcal E(-1)$ and take derived pushforward to the second factor. The standard finite affine cover computes coherent cohomology by Čech [F5]; choose a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution of the resulting bounded complex. DC, obtained from AC by [F3], supplies compatible resolution comparisons. Filtering this one total complex in the two orders gives the first and second spectral sequences [F3]; the identity comparison of the total complex identifies their abutment and canonical edge maps. Thus no arbitrary splitting is used. By steps 3.1 and 5.1, all rows except $q=1$ vanish. The surviving row is $H^1(\mathcal E(-2))\mathcal O(-2)\to H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)\mathcal O(-1)\to H^1(\mathcal E(-1))\mathcal O$. Its only cohomology is $\mathcal E(-1)$ in the middle because the diagonal resolution transforms $\mathcal E(-1)$ to itself. Twisting by $\mathcal O(1)$ gives the displayed monad. The dimensions are exactly those from steps 4.1–3.2. [F3, F5, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 1.2, algebra]

7.1 For a finite-type algebraic base $S$, tensor the relative diagonal Koszul resolution by the flat family and use the assumed base-change isomorphisms [A1]. The direct-image terms are vector bundles of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, and the finite filtered complex commutes with residue-field restriction. On every fiber, steps 1.1–5.1 give the monad. The right end map is surjective on every fiber, hence surjective by Nakayama [F8], and its kernel $K$ is locally free. Locally on $S$, write the remaining exact sequence as $0\to P^{-1}\to K\to\mathcal E\to0$, with $P^{-1}$ and $K$ flat over the base. Tensoring by any residue field $k(s)$ stays injective at the left because the fiber complex is a monad on the whole projective plane. Thus $\operatorname{Tor}_1^{\mathcal O_{S,s}}(k(s),\mathcal E)=0$, equivalently the maximal-ideal multiplication map is injective. Since $\mathcal E$ is finite over the local ring of $\mathbb P^2\times S$, [F6] proves flatness over $S$. The same base-change maps identify the relative middle cohomology with the given family. This is precisely the family range stated and does not assert base change outside it. [A1, F1, F3, F6, F8, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The raw ADHM convention and $ζ>0$.

[F1] In dimension one, stability is $I\ne0$, the complex equation is $IJ=0$, and the real equation is $|I|^2-|J|^2=\zeta$. [[def-qftx-adhm-linear-data-stability-and-regularity]]

[F2] Positive real-FI orbits correspond to stable complex data; zero real-FI stable data are exactly the regular locus. [[thm-qftx-adhm-real-complex-quotient-correspondence]]

[F3] Stable data yield the stated framed monad, and its sheaf is locally free exactly for costable data. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

[F4] $S^3$ is simply connected and every connected cover of it is trivial. [[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]], [[cor-connected-cover-of-a-simply-connected-space-is-trivial]]

[F5] Smooth partitions of unity exist under countable choice, and solutions to smooth ODEs depend smoothly on initial data and parameters. Full AC supplies countable choice. [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]], [[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F6] Stokes applies on the compact oriented four-sphere under countable choice. [[thm-general-stokes-theorem]], [[def-countable-choice]]



**Given:** $V=W=\mathbb C$, with the standard Hermitian structures.

1.1 Since stability says $I\ne0$, $IJ=0$ forces $J=0$. The real equation is then $|I|^2=\zeta$, so $I$ lies on the circle of radius $\sqrt\zeta$. The $U(1)$ gauge action multiplies $I$ by its phase and leaves scalar $B_1,B_2$ unchanged. It is transitive on that circle with trivial stabilizer; hence the quotient is exactly the unconstrained pair $(B_1,B_2)\in\mathbb C^2$. By [F2], this is the positive-FI stable quotient. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 At zero real level, $J=0$ still follows from $I\ne0$ and $IJ=0$, while the real equation becomes $|I|^2=0$. This contradicts $I\ne0$, so the stable zero-level locus is empty. In the positive chamber, $J=0$ makes all of $V$ a nonzero invariant subspace in $\ker J$; the data are not costable. By [F3], their framed sheaves are not locally free. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Let $P\to S^4$ be any smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle. Smooth local connection forms glue by a smooth partition of unity [F5]. Parallel transport from the center of each closed hemisphere along radial segments gives a smooth trivialization: each transported frame solves a linear smooth ODE, and [F5] supplies its smooth dependence on the endpoint. Their transition is a map $g:S^3\to U(1)$. Pulling back the universal cover $\mathbb R\to U(1)$ gives a covering of $S^3$; its connected component through a chosen point is a connected cover, hence is one-sheeted by [F4]. Thus $g$ lifts to $\theta:S^3\to\mathbb R$. Since the covering is a local diffeomorphism and $g$ is smooth, the lift is smooth. The homotopy $\theta_s=(1-s)\theta+s\theta(x_0)$ makes $g$ null-homotopic. Reparameterize this homotopy to be constant near its final parameter and use it on a collar of one hemisphere; this changes that trivialization so the transition is constant and the local frames glue to a global frame. Hence $P$ is trivial. In that frame write the real connection form as $a$ and its curvature as $f=da$, so $df=0$. Then $f\wedge f=d(a\wedge f)$, and Stokes [F6] gives $\int_{S^4}f\wedge f=0$. If it is ASD, $f=-*f$, so $f\wedge f=-f\wedge *f=-|f|^2d\mathrm{vol}$. The zero integral forces $f=0$, and the charge in the Statement is zero. Thus no smooth charge-one $U(1)$ ASD connection exists, and that empty ordinary sector cannot equal the positive-FI quotient $\mathbb C^2$. [F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** $N\ge1$, $k=0$, and the local ADHM definitions.

[F1] For $V=0$, every endomorphism and map to or from $V$ is unique; stability and costability are vacuous, and $GL(0)$ and $U(0)$ are trivial. [[def-qftx-adhm-linear-data-stability-and-regularity]]

[F2] The ADHM-to-monad construction uses source $V\mathcal O(-1)$, middle $(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O$, target $V\mathcal O(1)$, and the displayed Hilbert polynomial. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]



**Given:** The zero vector space $V=\mathbb C^0$.

1.1 There is exactly one linear map between any of the zero spaces, so $B_1,B_2,I,J$ are all zero maps. The complex and real equations are equalities between zero endomorphisms. The span of the empty family is $0=V$, and no nonzero subspace of $V$ exists; hence stability and costability hold. The gauge groups have one element, so each quotient consists of one point. [F1, algebra]

2.1 Substituting $V=0$ into the monad leaves $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its kernel at the right is $W\mathcal O$ and the image at the left is zero, so the middle cohomology is canonically $W\mathcal O$. Restriction to $L_\infty$ is the identity framing on the prescribed basis of $W$. Since $\chi(\mathcal O(m))=\binom{m+2}{2}$, its Hilbert polynomial is $N\binom{m+2}{2}$, the case $k=0$ of [F2]. No Euler-block or empty-matrix convention changes these calculations. [F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
